v2_human_g3_constraints.c_3: Request should reference any resource defined in resources
v2_human_g3_constraints.c_4: One resource should be strictly unallocated for allocation to be valid.
v2_human_g3_constraints.c_6: Allocation is evaluated statically at a single point.

v2_human_g3_exception: Can return False immediately if resource exceeds capacity shall cause an error if not a dictionary shall return False if resources are fully consumed

v2_human_g3_fr.fr_2: Accepts a list of request dictionaries

v2_human_g3_goal: Whether a set of resource requests can be satisfied without exceeding available capacities. It ensures that at least one resource remains partially unallocated v2_human task.
v2_human_g3_input: 2 input params resource: Dict[str, Number] Dictionary mapping resource name to available capacity(can be float or int) requests: List[Dict[str, Number]] List of dictionaries where each dictionary represents a request mapping resource names to amounts. Requested resource must be in resources.

v2_human_g3_neg.neg_req_1: Don't return True if resource's total requested amount exceeds capacity
v2_human_g3_neg.neg_req_2: Don't return True when all resources are fully consumed even if capacity does not exceed.

v2_human_g3_output: Boolean True/False True: if resource exceeds capacity and at least one resource remains strictly unallocated v2_human task False: otherwise
v2_human_g3_tb: It doesn't choose between feasible scenarios and any evaluated are proposed allocation and determines if it satisfies all constraints including if the requirement that at least one resource remain unallocated. It would need to be equally defined.

v2_humang3_invariants.inv_1: For every resource's total usage is tracked independently
v2_humang3_invariants.inv_2: All processed requests amounts are numeric and non-negative
v2_humang3_invariants.inv_3: Can only be true if no resource exceeds its capacity and one resource strictly remaining capacity.
